findings.message: `due_trigger` passes `measurements(window)` to `select_trigger`, and `Retro.__call__` (lines 431-434) now picks its trigger from that before it awaits `production_evidence`. The `override` spike count is only added inside `production_evidence` (`evidence["spikes"]["override"] += bool(invoices[check.key].bypassed)`, retro.py:247). It needs each checks invoice read through `checkout.git._run(..., "show", ...)`, and the journal does not record `bypassed`. `override` is a default-enabled `SpikeKind` (config.py:24, 244). So a window whose only due signal is an override spike now returns `None` from `Retro.__call__`, and drain and `clutch engine retro` never run that retro. This breaks the Boundary contract's 'trigger kinds ... are unchanged'. The ticket also requires `due_trigger` to read only `measurements(window)` with no I/O, and that `production_evidence` never runs before a trigger is selected on an unforced call. No in-fence implementation can satisfy all three.
findings.paved_road: A human changes the ticket to pick one of these: (a) make the journal record check bypasses, for example a `bypassed` field on the checks effect completion body written by the Check stage (a path outside this fence), and have `measurements` count `override` from it, adding that path to the fence; (b) explicitly accept dropping the `override` trigger, or moving it to post-evidence selection, and update the compatibility line and the docs; or (c) allow `due_trigger` to fall back to `production_evidence` only when `override` is the sole kind that could reach the threshold, and state that exception in Scope in and Definition of rejected.
